note: SNG-140: the TANGLED substrate — wild nanites AND living current together, kept by no one. The Wild Half's deep-power (fae/demonic/ruin, ring 2-4). Where the Continuous keep the fabricated deep in disciplined form and the Rootkin tend the living current, the Wild Half channels BOTH, undisciplined — potent but 'nothing twice, nothing where you left it.' `wildVariance:true` marks abilities whose outcome carries an uncontrolled element (CCode wires the variance resolver; until then the wildness lives in the fiction). A THIRD keeper-kind, NOT antipodal to the others — a different relationship to the substrate (tangled/wild), not a different pole.

abilities.name: Churn's Gift
abilities.narrationHints: You offer the working and it BLOOMS — generous, dazzling, exactly what was needed and never once what you asked for, the tangled current improvising on your intent like a musician who heard the tune only once.
abilities.description: The first wild-current working of the fae — a gift shaped from the tangled substrate, potent and giving, but it comes out its OWN way. The Wild Half does not obey; it accretes, it improvises, it gives you something better or stranger than you aimed for. Nobody is driving, and that is the gift and the danger both.
abilities.notFor: It gives, it does not command — you cannot aim it precisely; the current decides the details. And a gift from the Churn is real but never quite controllable; take what it offers, not what you meant to ask for.

tree.name: Churn's Gift
tree.grants: Shape a potent working from the wild substrate — generous and strong, but never exactly as aimed.
tree.cannot: You cannot control its precise form, it gives its own way rather than yours, and the wild current owes you nothing — it may give more than you asked, or sideways to it.

tree.name: Larger Asking
tree.grants: Ask more of the Churn and it gives more. You may now name the SHAPE of what you want — a weapon, a warmth, a way through — and the wild current will honour the shape even as it invents every detail you did not name.
tree.cannot: The shape holds; nothing inside it does. Ask larger and the sideways-ness grows with the gift — a bigger asking is a stranger answer, never a safer one.

tree.name: What the Churn Remembers
tree.grants: The wild current begins to know you. Gifts arrive UNASKED at the edge of need — not reliably, never on command, but often enough that churnfolk speak of being kept. What it gives you, you may hand onward to another, and it keeps giving in their hands.
tree.cannot: Being known by the Churn runs both directions; it takes an interest, and the GM decides what that means. An unasked gift arrives on the current's timing and is never the one you would have chosen.

mechanic.note: T-III construct with the roster's HIGHEST variance: 'generous and strong, but NEVER EXACTLY AS AIMED.' The craft's identity IS its unreliability.

abilities.name: Wild Flowering
abilities.narrationHints: Life and ruin at once — growth erupting where you touched, blooming and rotting and blooming again, the fabricated and the living currents tangled past any telling which is which, and none of it where you left it a moment ago.
abilities.description: The deeper wild working — the tangled substrate let loose as growth-and-decay together, life and unmaking in one uncontrolled flowering. The fae art of nothing-twice: a burst of wild creation that is also wild dissolution, potent and beautiful and impossible to hold in one shape.
abilities.notFor: It creates and unmakes at once, uncontrolled — you cannot get pure growth or pure ruin from it, only the tangle. And what it makes does not stay made; the Wild Flowering is nothing-where-you-left-it given form.

tree.name: Wild Flowering
tree.grants: Unleash a wild flowering of tangled growth-and-ruin — potent, beautiful, and beyond precise control.
tree.cannot: It cannot be aimed at pure creation or pure destruction, what it makes will not hold its shape, and the wild current, once opened, flowers where IT wills, not only where you meant.

tree.name: Long Flowering
tree.grants: The flowering takes a district rather than a room, and what it makes now lasts — days rather than moments — before the tangle takes it back. Long enough to shelter in, to harvest from, to be changed by.
tree.cannot: You still cannot aim it at pure growth or pure ruin; the larger the flowering, the more of both arrives. What lasts longer takes longer to unmake and unmakes harder when it goes. And a district that has flowered is not the district it was.

mechanic.note: T-IV, incapacitating. r1: a wild flowering of tangled growth-and-ruin — potent, beautiful, BEYOND PRECISE CONTROL

abilities.name: Honest Bargain
abilities.narrationHints: You name the terms and they are FAIR — scrupulously, horrifyingly fair — and the tangled current seals them, and now the bargain will keep itself, in ways neither of you can fully predict or take back.
abilities.description: The Wild Half's demonic bargain — a pact struck from the tangled substrate, honest in its terms (the Abyssals bargain fairly; that is the horror) but wild in its keeping. Once sealed, the bargain runs its own way, fair to the letter and uncontrollable in the fulfilling. Appetite made a contract nobody is driving.
abilities.notFor: It binds only a struck bargain — no bargain, no bond; and it is scrupulously FAIR, which is the danger, not the safety. Once sealed, neither party fully controls how the wild current fulfills it; the terms hold, the manner runs wild.

tree.name: Honest Bargain
tree.grants: Seal a fair but wild bargain that keeps itself — the terms exact, the fulfilling uncontrollable.
tree.cannot: It needs a genuine bargain to bind, it is fair to the letter (which is the horror), and once sealed it fulfills its terms its OWN way — you cannot take it back, and you cannot fully steer how it comes due.

tree.name: Standing Bargain
tree.grants: A bargain may be struck now with what is not a person — a place, a current, a thing that simply persists — and it may be set to outlive both parties, passing to heirs and successors who never sat at the table.
tree.cannot: It is still scrupulously fair, which at this scale is considerably worse. A bargain with a place is kept by the place, in the place's own understanding of the terms. And a pact that outlives you is a pact you cannot renegotiate.

abilities.name: Collection
abilities.narrationHints: There is no violence in it. There is a debt, and a date, and the date arrives.
abilities.description: ⚠️ THE MAW'S CRAFT — the tradition's own bound turned into a killing. `the_offered_price` says COLLECTING IS NOT OPTIONAL. When what was priced was a life, the collection is a death, and the abyssal does not perform it angrily. They perform it on schedule.
abilities.notFor: Anyone who owes you nothing. ⚠️ It requires a REAL, PRIOR bargain in which a life was the named price — you cannot invent the debt, and the terms can be shown. That honesty does not make it better.

tree.name: Collection
tree.grants: BIND the named price and collect it — a life pledged against a struck bargain. The collection strikes the pledged party wherever they stand, and a life pledged is a life ended. It arrives however it arrives.
tree.cannot: Any debt not actually incurred. Choosing the manner.

tree.name: Standing Account
tree.grants: BIND it across distance and time — neither of you needs to be present when it closes.
tree.cannot: Being elsewhere as an alibi: everyone knows who held the account.

mechanic.note: ⚠️ GATED ON A PRIOR BARGAIN — cannot open a fight, only close an account. The engine should refuse it without a recorded debt.

tree.cannot: Depending on them; under real need the odds worsen.

tree.cannot: Holding a true line against the drift without paying extra.

tree.cannot: Giving them to more than a few, or to anyone unwilling.

abilities.plainly: A travel, chase and explore action, learned rather than inherited — anyone with churnfolk training flies this way, whatever they are. Rank 1 is short flights: over a wall, across a river, out of a fall. Rank 2 flies a whole leg and roughly halves its days, though you drift toward where the churn is going unless you pay to hold a line. Rank 3 gives wings to the rest of the party for a shorter span each. The catch is reliability rather than danger: needing them badly makes them less likely to come, and a failure grounds you rather than dropping you.
